The cover image appears in lists, and images are copied into the built site.\n- **S2: Hosted admin console behind the security gate**\n  - **Blocked by:** T01–T09 and S1\n  - **Delivers:** ADR-003 superseding ADR-001 for the console, an updated `CLAUDE.md` rule, rate-limited login, HTTPS, no default accounts, and the admin password from the environment.\n\nT04, T05, T07 and T08 can be worked in any order once their blockers close, but the per-ticket runbook takes one at a time.\n\n**Questions:**\n- **Granularity.** The biggest tickets are T03, T04 and T06. They had to be combined to stay within 9. Do any feel too large?\n- **Blocking edges.** Does T06 genuinely need T04? I put it there so \"the live Guide stays on the site while a Revision waits\" can be tested against a real build. The same goes for T07 needing T04 to render markers on the site.\n- **Images as stretch.** Images are central for your client, but the rubric counts \"media uploads with alt text\" as stretch, and stretch only counts once core is ≥70. Caching would make the refusal path harder to follow. |\n162\t| 8 | `review_step` duplicates `workflow_step`. | **Not changed.** They differ on purpose. `workflow_step` saves the editor form and shows the editor on refusal. `review_step` carries Review notes and shows the review screen with the notes kept. Merging them would need a callback for each difference. |\n163\t| 9 | `sent_review_notes` silently dropped non-text fields (e.g. a file posted as `quote`), so Unpublish could go ahead with fewer notes than were sent. | **Fixed.** A non-text field counts as blank, so a half-filled row reaches `app/guides.py` and is refused. After these changes: pyright 0 errors; `pytest` 174 passed.\n177\t\n178\t\n179\t######## #6 T05 — Admins Return or Unpublish Guides with Review notes | Avulpix0412 2026-10-17T20:48:07Z | closed 2026-10-17T20:50:01Z\n180\tAfter the first round, I let Claude code do two revisions, .Firstly, quotes have to match when they cross formatting. Typically a long guide can easily go back and forth two or three times, so with the old rule if the editor missed something from round 1 and the admin didn't repeat it in round 2, the old highlight would disappear and the problem could easily end up in the published guide. So my choice is to keep all rounds visible, and with the newest round standing out, which will not confused the editor which has been dealt with already and which is still yet to solved.\n182\t\n183\t######## #7 T06 — Editors revise or delete their Published Guides | Avulpix0412 2026-10-17T21:18:03Z | closed 2026-10-18T00:26:41Z\n184\t## `/code-review` findings for T06 and how each was resolved\n185\t\n186\t| # | Finding | Resolution |\n187\t|---|---------|------------|\n188\t| 1 | **No migration:** the new columns (`guides.trashed_at`, `restored_at`, `review_rounds.revision_id`) never reach a database made before T06, and the new index fails on every connect (`no such column: revision_id`). The local `cms.db` from T05 would 500 on every page. | **Fixed.** `db.connect()` now adds any missing column listed in `ADDED_COLUMNS` (`ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN`) before creating indexes on them. To keep every change additive, a Revision's Return is now `kind = 'return'` with `revision_id` set, rather than a new `kind`, since a CHECK can't be altered in place. `revision_id` has no foreign key, and Revision ids are never reused (`AUTOINCREMENT`). Test: `test_a_database_made_before_revisions_and_the_trash_still_works`. Also checked on a copy of the T05 `cms.db`. |\n189\t| 2 | **A Revision can undo newer changes:** it is copied from the Guide when opened, so Publishing it later replaces an Admin's direct edit, or a Guide that was Unpublished, changed and Published again. | **Fixed, as a warning.** A Revision records the Guide's `updated_at` when it is opened. If the Guide changed since, the review screen and the Revision editor say so (\"在这份修订打开之后，攻略又被修改过…发布…那些修改会丢失\"). The Admin decides. Refusing outright would leave the Editor stuck with no way to bring the Revision up to date. Test: `test_the_review_screen_warns_when_the_guide_changed_after_the_revision_opened`. |\n190\t| 3 | **Pending count misses a deletion for good:** a Published Guide deleted to the Trash and then deleted for good before the next build vanishes from `changes_not_on_site`, while the site still shows it. | **Fixed.** Deleting a Published Guide for good records it in a new `removed_guides` table, which the count includes. Deleting and restoring between builds still counts as a change. That overcounts, the safer error, as in T05. Test: `test_deleting_a_published_guide_for_good_stays_a_change_not_on_the_site`. |\n191\t| 4 | **Unpublish silently turns a Submitted Revision back into a Draft** without touching its `updated_at`. | **Fixed** (`updated_at` now moves, and only a Submitted Revision is touched). Keeping the Revision is deliberate: there is nothing for it to change while the Guide is off the site, so it can't be Submitted until the Guide is Published again (\"修订只能在攻略重新发布后提交\"). The new console and site pages were checked with `/browse` at 1280px and 390px: `scrollWidth` is 390 on every page at 390px.\n299\t\n300\t\n301\t######## #10 T09 — Admins manage users | Avulpix0412 2026-10-18T01:08:45Z | closed 2026-10-18T01:16:17Z\n302\t## `/code-review` findings for T09, and how each was resolved\n303\t\n304\tThe review covered the uncommitted T09 work: the Users page, the account page, the lockout guards and the console 403 page.\n305\t\n306\t| # | Finding | Resolution |\n307\t|---|---|---|\n308\t| 1 | `can_open_revision` (and `can_submit`) still offer the 修订 / 提交审核 buttons to a banned Editor, who is then refused. | **Kept the buttons, as designed:** story 76 wants a banned Editor told *why*, not left with a button that silently went missing. The refusal re-renders the editor with the reason. **Changed:** the reason now also appears up front, on every console page a banned Editor opens (`accounts.SUBMISSION_BANNED`, shown from `base.html`), so they see it before clicking. Test: `test_a_banned_editor_keeps_drafting_but_submit_and_revisions_are_refused_with_the_reason`. |\n309\t| 2 | `ban_submissions`, `lift_submission_ban` and `reactivate` read the state with one query, then UPDATE without re-checking it, so a change another Admin makes in between (e.g. a Deactivation) could be overwritten. | **Fixed.** Each UPDATE repeats its precondition in the WHERE clause (`AND state = …`, `AND role = 'editor'`), and refuses when no row changes (`CHANGED_MEANWHILE`). Promotion to Admin does the same against a concurrent ban. This matches how the last-Admin guard already worked. |\n310\t| 3 | The Users page needs `manage_users`, but calls `guides.counts_by_author`, which checked `manage_all_guides` and raised a `guides.NotAllowed` nothing caught. | **Fixed.** `counts_by_author` exists only for the Users page, so it now checks `manage_users`. |\n311\t| 4 | `user_manager` was a fourth copy of the \"signed in + capability, else `AdminRequired`\" guard. | **Fixed.** `web.requires(capability)` builds every guard: `admin_user`, `trash_manager`, `site_builder` and `user_manager`. Each guard it makes is recorded in `web.ADMIN_GUARDS`. The access-control test now finds guarded routes through that set rather than a list of function names, so a route behind any future guard is covered automatically (21 routes today). |\n312\t| 5 | `accounts.NotAllowed` and `routes/users.status_for` duplicate `guides.NotAllowed` and `routes/guides.status_for`. | **Not changed in T09.** Merging the two `Refused` hierarchies touches every Guide route, which is a refactor of its own. The concrete gap the review pointed to (a `guides.NotAllowed` escaping a Users route) is gone with #3. |\n313\t| 6 | `status_for` had a dead `AccountNotFound` branch, and the lookup-then-404 code was repeated three times. | **Fixed.** One `shown_account()` helper does the lookup and the 404; the dead branch is removed. |\n314\t| 7 | The account page counts every Author's Guides to read one Author's counts. | **Not changed.** The site has a handful of Authors, so this is one small GROUP BY per page view. If it ever matters, it is a one-line change. |\n315\t| 8 | Every account mutator re-read and returned the account, and the only caller threw it away. | **Fixed.** The mutators return `None`. |\n316\t| 9 | `GET /admin/users/{id}/deactivate` showed \"are you sure?\" even for yourself or an account already Deactivated, and posting it was then refused. | **Fixed.** `accounts.check_deactivatable` refuses before the confirmation, and the account page is shown with the reason (400). Test: `test_an_admin_cannot_deactivate_themselves`. |\n317\t| 10 | Templates hard-coded `minlength=\"8\"` and \"至少 8 个字符\". | **Fixed.** `min_password_length` is a template global from `accounts.MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH`, used on the Users page, the account page and first-login setup. |\n318\t\n319\tThe review also confirmed these hold:\n320\t- the removed T01 deactivation test is covered by T09's test through the real Users page;\n321\t- nothing calls the removed `set_state` any more;\n322\t- every new form carries the CSRF token, and every new link is relative;\n323\t- no password is logged or flashed;\n324\t- `users.last_login_at` is in `ADDED_COLUMNS`.\n325\t\n326\t## Decisions not spelled out in the spec\n327\t\n328\t- **Temporary passwords are typed by the Admin** (at least 8 characters), when creating an account and when resetting a password. The server never shows or stores one in plain text.\n329\t- **A password reset** also ends the user's open sessions. An Admin can't reset their own password. First-login setup then offers the user's current Display name, so a reset doesn't force a new one.\n330\t- **A Submission ban is for Editors only**, since Admins Publish without Submitting. To promote a banned Editor, the ban must be lifted first.\n331\t- **A banned Editor can't open a Revision** either, because they could never Submit it. Before T09, only Submit checked the ban.\n332\t- **Reactivating an account returns it to the normal state.** A ban from before the deactivation is not kept, and the confirmation page says so.\n333\t- **The last-active-Admin guard is part of the database update itself.** No console request can reach it: an Admin able to act is active, so the target is never the last Admin. It protects against two Admins removing each other at the same moment. It is tested in two ways:\n334\t  - through HTTP: once A deactivates B, B's session is dead, so B can't deactivate A;\n335\t  - with one direct call into `app/accounts.py` using a stale Admin, which is the only way to reach the guard. The user agreed to this exception to Seam 1.\n336\t- **Editors refused on Admin routes** now get a console page (403) that keeps the navigation and logout, not plain text.\n337\t- **Users page Guide counts** show \"已发布 N · 共 M\", where M counts Guides in every status outside the Trash.\n338\t- **Last-login times are UTC**, like every other console timestamp.\n339\t- **Schema:** `users.last_login_at` was added the additive way. A test with the pre-T09 users table checks it, and fails if the migration line is removed.\n340\t\n341\tVerification: `uv run pytest -q` gives 263 passed, and pyright reports 0 errors.\n342\t\n343\t\n344\t######## #11 S1 — Image uploads with alt text and cover images | Avulpix0412 2026-10-18T04:59:41Z | closed 2026-10-18T05:59:36Z\n345\t## S1 `/code-review` findings and how each was resolved\n346\t\n347\tThe review covered the uncommitted S1 changes against `HEAD`. It reported 10 findings without verifying them; I checked each one against the code.\n348\t\n349\t| # | Finding | Resolution |\n350\t|---|---|---|\n351\t| 1 | **Enter key presses an image button.** The image section (its 删除这张图片 and 上传 buttons) sat inside the editor form before 保存. A browser's Enter key presses a form's first submit button, so Enter in a text field could delete the first image, or fail an empty upload and lose the typed text. | **Fixed.** In all three editors (Guide, Revision, Tournament item), the image section now comes after the main buttons. The section has its own 保存说明和封面 button. New test: `test_pressing_enter_in_an_editor_form_saves_it_rather_than_pressing_an_image_button` (guide, revision, tournament). |\n352\t| 2 | **Files change outside the transaction.** Image files were written and deleted inside the open SQLite transaction, so a rollback could leave the disk and the database disagreeing. | **Fixed.** New `db.after_commit(conn, committed=…, rolled_back=…)`. A new upload's file is removed if the transaction rolls back. A file whose last row is deleted goes only after the commit. No agreed seam can make a transaction fail mid-way, so this was checked once with a throwaway script (a rollback removes the new file; a failed delete keeps the old one) and not committed as a test. |\n353\t| 3 | **Overflowing alt-text id.** `alt_zh_<huge number>` overflowed SQLite and gave a 500. | **Fixed.** The id goes through `id_or_none`. Test: `test_a_tampered_alt_text_field_is_ignored`. |\n354\t| 4 | **No request size limit.** The whole multipart body is received and spooled before the 5 MB check. | **Kept, docstring corrected.** The console runs on one machine (ADR-001), so nothing limits request size yet. A body-size limit belongs to the hosted console, #12 (S2). |\n355\t| 5 | **\"Still in use\" was a substring test.** Mentioning the file name in prose blocked deletion. | **Fixed.** Only a Markdown image reference `![…](<filename>)` counts. Test: `test_a_file_name_mentioned_in_prose_does_not_stop_its_image_being_deleted`. |\n356\t| 6 | **Stale cover name.** Deleting the cover image leaves its name in the `cover` column. | **No change.** File names are random and never reused, so the stale name can never match again. `media.cover` falls back to the first image, which is the documented default whenever the chosen cover is gone. |\n357\t| 7 | **Duplicated logic** between Guide and Tournament image functions and routes. | **Kept.** Each module turns a `media.BadImage` into its own `Refused`, which is the existing split between `guides.py` and `content.py`. The routes follow each router's existing save-then-act pattern. The shared logic (checks, storage, the in-use test) lives in `media.py`. |\n358\t| 8 | **Repeated queries.** `copy_files` queried images again. | **Fixed.** The Site build passes the images it already loaded. The per-owner lookups (`image`, `file`, `checked_cover`) scan only one owner's handful of images, so they stay as they are. |\n359\t| 9 | **Duplicated save check.** `save` repeated the `_editable` + `can_edit` check. | **Fixed.** `save` calls `_changeable`. |\n360\t| 10 | **Glossary drift.** The glossary listed \"media\" and \"thumbnail\" under _Avoid_, yet the code uses them. | **Fixed.** `CONTEXT.md` now says that \"media folder\" is only where Images' files are stored, and drops \"thumbnail\" from the list. The site CSS comment says \"a small Cover image\". |\n361\t\n362\t## Choices the user made at the start\n363\t\n364\t- **Scope: Guides and Tournament items.** Tournament items get images, alt text, and an optional cover (a 不用封面 choice). A Guide's cover is its first image unless the writer chooses another.\n365\t- **Commits** start `S1:`, and `.claude/state/phase` reads `S1`.\n366\t- **Inserting an image:** each image shows its code `![](<file name>)`, with 插入中文正文 and 插入英文正文 buttons that add it at the cursor. Without script, the writer copies the code by hand.\n367\t- **Deleting an image the saved text uses** is refused, naming which text uses it.\n368\t- **Seam 3 (this ticket only):** tests may list file names in the media folder, to show that nothing escapes it and that deleted images are gone.\n369\t\n370\t## Decisions made while building\n371\t\n372\t- **Revisions** carry their own copy of the images, alt text and cover, as the spec requires. The rows are copied, the files shared. Publishing the Revision replaces the Guide's images; discarding it leaves them alone.\n373\t- **Storage:** the media folder is `CMS_MEDIA`, which defaults to `media/` next to the database (git-ignored). Each test therefore gets its own media folder.\n374\t- **Upload and delete save the form too.** Their buttons sit inside the editor form and save the rest of it in the same transaction, like the workflow buttons, so unsaved text is never lost. If either step is refused, nothing is saved.\n375\t- **Content checks:** files are recognised by their first bytes (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF), and the stored extension comes from the content. Console responses carry `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.\n376\t- **Alt text:** a language's saved alt text wins. If it is empty, the alt written in the Markdown is used.\n377\t- **Site build:** it copies the images of Published, non-Trash Guides and Tournament items to `site/media/`, which both trees share. Covers show on home, Hero, Author and Guides-index list items, and in the 锦标赛 list.\n378\t- **Image changes count as site changes.** Uploading or deleting an image counts as a change on Published content, so it appears in \"N 项更改尚未更新到网站\".\n379\t\n380\t## Tests\n381\t\n382\t- 482 passed in total. pyright reports 0 errors (`tests/test_s1_images.py` has been added to the typecheck command).\n383\t- **Mutation checks:** I broke the code on purpose for slices whose tests passed at first run. Every mutation made a test fail:\n384\t  - content check removed, size check off by one, uploaded name kept;\n385\t  - visibility check and save check removed;\n386\t  - cover choice ignored or forgotten, no first-image default;\n387\t  - \"still in use\" check removed, files kept on delete;\n388\t  - no change stamp after an image change.\n389\t- **Visual check** with `/browse` at 1280px and 390px: the Guide editor's image section, the home list with a cover, and the Guide page. `scrollWidth` is 390 at 390px.\n390\t\n391\t\n392\t######## #15 A Hero's Slug stays fixed when its names are corrected | Avulpix0412 2026-10-17T17:46:24Z | closed 2026-10-17T17:47:32Z\n393\t## `/code-review` findings (medium) and how each was resolved\n394\t\n395\tScope: this branch's changes for #15. The edit keeps a Hero's Slug, and no two Heroes share an English Official name (checked on add and on edit).\n396\t\n397\t| # | Finding | Resolution |\n398\t|---|---------|------------|\n399\t| 1 | `templates/admin/hero_edit.html` still said the slug follows the English Official name (\"网址名会跟随官方英文名自动更新\"). | **Fixed.** It now says \"网址名在添加英雄时生成，之后修改名称也不会改变。\" |\n400\t| 2 | With the Slug fixed, an old misspelled Slug can block a later real Hero. Add `Vanesa` (slug `vanesa`) and correct it to `Vanessa`. Adding a real Hero named `Vanesa` is then refused, and there's no way past it, because Hero Slugs can't be edited and get no `-n` suffix. | **Deferred.** It needs a decision between a `-n` suffix like Guides and letting Admins edit a Hero's Slug. It only happens when a misspelling matches another real Hero's name. The refusal message names the Hero holding the Slug. |\n401\t| 3 | In add, the Slug check ran before the English-name check, so the same duplicate got a different message on add than on edit. | **Fixed.** The English-name check runs first on both paths. `test_a_hero_whose_slug_is_already_taken_is_refused` now uses `Vanessa!` (a different name that gives the same Slug). New test: `test_a_new_hero_with_another_heros_english_name_is_refused`. |\n402\t| 4 | The English-name rule is checked in application code only, with no `UNIQUE` index on `(kind, lower(name_en))`. | **Not changed.** The console is local and used by a single Admin, so a race is very unlikely. An index would also stop startup on any local database that already has duplicates. SQLite's `lower()` is ASCII-only too (see 5). |\n403\t| 5 | SQLite's `lower()` folds only ASCII, so `Éclair` and `ÉCLAIR` weren't caught. | **Fixed.** The comparison now uses Python's `str.casefold()`. New test: `test_english_names_clash_ignoring_non_ascii_case_too`. |\n404\t| 6 | The `app/game.py` module docstring didn't say the Slug is set only once. | **Fixed.** It now says the Slug is derived once, when the Hero is added, and never changes after that. |\n405\t| 7 | The help text in `templates/admin/heroes.html` didn't say the Slug is fixed after creation. | **Fixed.** It now says \"网址名在添加时由英文名生成，之后不再改变。\" |\n406\t| 8 | `test_editing_only_the_chinese_name_keeps_the_heros_own_slug` is now redundant. The add-path duplicate message had no test. | **Partly fixed.** The add-path test was added (see 3). The Chinese-name test is kept because it still checks that a Chinese-only edit succeeds. |\n407\t\n408\t**Verification:** `tests/test_t02_heroes_patches.py` and `tests/test_t03_guides.py` pass (71 tests). Pyright reports 0 errors on `app/game.py` and the T02 tests. The full suite still has 14 failures, all in `tests/test_ctx_guard.py` and `tests/test_usage_report.py`. Those files aren't touched by this change, and the `test_usage_report.py` failures also happen with the change set aside.\n409\t\n410\t\n411\t######## #15 A Hero's Slug stays fixed when its names are corrected | Avulpix0412 2026-10-17T19:27:20Z | closed 2026-10-17T17:47:32Z\n412\tI kept the slug fixed when a Hero's name is corrected so that links stay easy to use. When someone shares the link, they won't be worried that it doesn't work afterwards. I also said that duplicate names should  be refused, because two Heroes with the same name would confuse readers.\n413\t\n414\t######## #18 Admin console templates use root-absolute paths | Avulpix0412 2026-10-17T19:01:56Z | closed 2026-10-17T19:02:47Z\n415\t## `/code-review` findings (medium) and resolutions\n416\t\n417\tReviewed the uncommitted diff for this issue. 6 findings; 2 fixed, 4 left as they are.\n418\t\n419\t| # | Finding | Resolution |\n420\t|---|---|---|\n421\t| 1 | **`app/web.py` `console_root`:** Starlette includes `root_path` in `request.url.path`, so if the console is mounted under a prefix (e.g. `--root-path /cms`), the `../` chain climbs past it and every console link drops the prefix. | **Fixed.** `console_root` strips `request.scope[\"root_path\"]` before counting. `test_the_link_prefix_leads_back_to_the_console_root` now runs every depth with and without a `/cms` mount. |\n422\t| 2 | **`tests/test_console_links.py` `check_page`:** any 403 on a bare POST counted as \"route exists\", so the Guide filter form (`method=\"get\"`) was never checked with a GET, and the 405 branch could not run. | **Fixed.** `check_page` reads which forms are `method=\"get\"` and checks their actions with a GET (expects 200). Every other form target must answer an empty POST with the CSRF 403. The 405 branch is gone. |\n423\t| 3 | **Altitude:** one `<base href>` in `admin/base.html` could replace about 30 prefixed links. | **Not changed.** The link-prefix approach was the chosen design for this issue. `<base>` also changes how every relative URL on the page resolves, fragment links included. The crawl test catches any link that is missing its prefix. |\n424\t| 4 | **`console_root(request)` is called once per link**, including per row in loops. | **Not changed.** It is one string operation per link, so the cost is negligible. Calling it inline keeps it the same shape as the existing `csrf_token(request)` global. |\n425\t| 5 | **Some assertions in the T01/T02/T03 tests are tied to one URL depth** (`../logout`, `../admin/heroes`, `../../../admin/guides/…/preview`). | **Not changed.** Each checks a specific page at a fixed URL. `test_console_links.py` covers whether links resolve on every console page. |\n426\t| 6 | **Redirects** (`home_for`, `login_required_handler`, `setup_required_handler`) still use root-absolute `Location` values. | **Not changed. Out of scope:** this issue covers HTML only, and its acceptance criteria exclude server-side `RedirectResponse` URLs. |\n427\t\n428\tAfter the fixes: `uv run pytest -q` → 150 passed. `scripts/check_submission.py --stage 1` → \"no root-absolute paths in HTML\" PASS. The only failing check is the compaction log, which is unrelated to this issue.\n429\t\n430\t######## #18 Admin console templates use root-absolute paths | Avulpix0412 2026-10-17T19:31:08Z | closed 2026-10-17T19:02:47Z\n431\tHere Claude asked me whether the console templates should be excluded from the check and I didn't want to it to be excluded. They are part of the project too, and making them use relative paths wasn't difficult to achieve, so it keeps the whole project consistent.\n432\t\n433\t######## #25 Show console and site times in Beijing time, not UTC | Avulpix0412 2026-10-18T01:17:39Z | closed 2026-10-18T04:04:18Z\n434\tAfter T06 is done, Claude code recommended me to do T07 first, but  I think it is better to do T09 first, because both the user page and the page an editor sees when access is refused depend on this and some stuff on the security checklist can only be tested once it is done, such as the deactivated user cannot log in.\n435\t\n436\t######## #25 Show console and site times in Beijing time, not UTC | Avulpix0412 2026-10-18T01:18:48Z | closed 2026-10-18T04:04:18Z\n437\tI changed the time of the web from UTC to Beijing time, because most of the admins, editors and readers will follow that time, and as this stage is not the only place with this problem, I let Claude figure this out separately.\n438\t\n439\t######## #25 Show console and site times in Beijing time, not UTC | Avulpix0412 2026-10-18T03:53:56Z | closed 2026-10-18T04:04:18Z\n440\t## `/code-review` findings for #25, and how each was resolved\n441\t\n442\tReviewed the uncommitted #25 changes. 6 findings, none breaking:\n443\t\n444\t1. **The users-page test could fail at a minute boundary.** The Admin signs in during the `admin` fixture, before `started` reads the clock, and `started` is rounded down to the minute. **Fixed:** `started` is now a minute before the test began. That still tells Beijing time from UTC, which is 8 hours off.\n445\t2. **Opt-in filters don't fully meet \"a new page can't show UTC by accident\".** A template could print `{{ x.published_at }}` without `|beijing_time`. **Fixed (user's choice: template scan test):** `test_no_template_prints_a_stored_time_without_converting_it` reads every template and fails on any `{{ …_at… }}` that doesn't go through `|beijing_time` or `|beijing_date`. Mutation check: putting `trashed_at[:16]` back into `trash.html` makes it fail.\n446\t3. **The filters crashed on a missing (NULL) time.** **Fixed:** `beijing_time(None)` and `beijing_date(None)` return `\"\"`, tested in `test_a_missing_time_shows_nothing_rather_than_breaking_the_page`.\n447\t4. **The scrolling-table test checks only the markup, not `scrollWidth`.** **Resolved by hand:** the stack has no automated browser, so the test checks that each table is inside `<div class=\"scroll\">`. With `/browse` at 390×844, `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` is **390** on the Guide list, the Trash and the dashboard, with long titles in place.\n448\t5. **Long Guide titles were forced onto one line** (`.scroll td { white-space: nowrap }`). **Fixed:** the title cells in the Guide list, Trash and review queue use the existing `td.wrap` class.\n449\t6. **The dashboard's review-queue table wasn't in a scrolling container.** **Fixed (user's choice: wrap it):** it's wrapped like the others and added to the scroll test.\n450\t\n451\t## Decisions made while building\n452\t\n453\t- **One conversion, two filters.** `app/times.py` has `beijing_time` (`2026-10-17 21:05`) and `beijing_date` (`2026-10-18`). Stored times and every comparison (the \"N 项更改尚未更新到网站\" count, the stale-Revision check, ordering) stay UTC.\n454\t- **A fixed UTC+8 offset, not `zoneinfo(\"Asia/Shanghai\")`.** China has had no DST since 1991, so the times come out the same, and Windows needs no tz database (that would mean a new dependency).\n455\t- **No \"北京时间\" label** on the times (user's choice).\n456\t- **Testing (user's choice):** the day-crossing cases (17:30 UTC → the next Beijing date, the New Year rollover, 15:59:59.999 keeping its day) are unit tests of the conversion function. Mutation check: if publishing a Revision doesn't touch `updated_at`, it fails.\n458\t- `CONTEXT.md` gains a **Beijing time (北京时间)** entry.\n459\t\n460\tTests: 439 passed. pyright: 0 errors.\n461\t\n462\t\n463\t"}]}}

The stored hashes are `$argon2id$`, and no plain password appeared in the server log.\n39\t\n40\t\n41\t######## #3 T02 — Admins manage Heroes and Patches | Avulpix0412 2026-10-17T12:10:39Z | closed 2026-10-17T12:42:03Z\n42\t## `/code-review` findings for T02 and how each was resolved\n43\t\n44\tTwo-axis review (Standards and Spec, run as separate sub-agents) of the T02 diff against `c868270`.\n45\t\n46\t### Standards (no hard violations)\n47\t\n48\t| Finding | Resolution |\n49\t|---|---|\n50\t| **Slug (网址名)** is a new domain word but missing from `CONTEXT.md` (CLAUDE.md: use the glossary vocabulary) | **Fixed.** Added a **Slug (网址名)** entry to `CONTEXT.md`. |\n51\t| `routes/game.py` re-trims the Patch name for the flash, because `game.add_patch` returned `None` | **Fixed.** `add_patch` now returns the `Patch` it created, the same way `add_hero` returns a `Hero`. |\n52\t| `_checked_hero` returns a cleaned tuple, not a Hero (Mysterious Name) | **Fixed.** Renamed to `_checked_names_and_slug`. |\n53\t| The seed script's `except game.Refused: continue` hid every refusal | **Fixed.** It now prints `left unchanged (<reason>)`, like the account seeding does. |\n54\t| `game.Refused` duplicates `accounts.Refused` | **Kept.** Each domain module owns its refusals, and routes catch them per module. Sharing one class would mean editing T01 code for no change in behaviour. |\n55\t| Three `*_page` helpers repeat `TemplateResponse(..., status_code=400 if error else 200)` | **Kept.** This matches the T01 `auth.py` pattern, and three short call sites don't justify a helper. |\n56\t| `name_zh, name_en` travel together (Data Clumps) | **Kept.** It is mild and matches T01's keyword-argument style. Revisit when the other Game Term kinds arrive. |\n57\t| The `kind = 'hero'` literal is repeated in SQL | **Kept.** Generalise when T-next adds the other six kinds, not before. |\n58\t| `patches.created_at` is never read | **Kept.** Every table has `created_at` (`users`, `sessions`). |\n59\t\n60\t### Spec (every acceptance criterion met; 25 T02 tests pass)\n61\t\n62\t| Finding | Resolution |\n63\t|---|---|\n64\t| Patch duplicates are caught by exact text only (`6.7`, `v6.7` and `6.70` all differ) | **Kept, as an open question.** The ticket only asks that an existing Patch be refused. A format rule (such as digits and dots only) can be a follow-up if wanted. |\n65\t| There is no way to correct a mistyped Patch | **Out of scope** for T02, which doesn't ask for editing or deleting Patches. Candidate follow-up ticket. |\n66\t| The `game_terms` CHECK already lists all seven kinds | **Kept.** `CONTEXT.md` defines Game Term as one of seven kinds, so the schema stores the concept rather than a Hero-only table. |\n67\t| A slug is re-derived when the English name is edited | **Kept, as a decision to confirm.** It follows \"derived from its English Official name\", and no public Hero pages exist yet. The only failures are the same 14 MP2 Exercise B stubs (`ctx_guard` and `usage_report`) as before. pyright: 0 errors.\n104\t\n105\t######## #5 T04 — The Site build puts Published Guides online in Chinese and English | Avulpix0412 2026-10-17T17:34:35Z | closed 2026-10-17T18:10:04Z\n106\t## Decision: a Hero's Slug is fixed once set\n107\t\n108\tA Hero's Slug is set once, from its English Official name, when the Hero is added (`Vanessa` → `vanessa`). It does **not** change when the English Official name is later corrected.\n109\t\n110\t**Why:** the Site build writes one page per Hero at that Slug, and every Guide's Slug starts with its Hero's (`vanessa-12`). If the Hero's Slug followed name corrections, published Hero pages would move and shared links would break.\n111\t\n112\t**This reverses what's there now:**\n113\t- `CONTEXT.md`, under **Slug**, says a Hero's Slug \"follows that name when it is corrected\".\n114\t- `edit_hero` in `app/game.py` recomputes the Slug on every name edit.\n115\t- `tests/test_t02_heroes_patches.py::test_admin_edits_a_heros_official_names_and_the_slug_follows` asserts the old behaviour.\n116\t\n117\tAll three need updating to match.\n118\t\n119\t\n120\t######## #5 T04 — The Site build puts Published Guides online in Chinese and English | Avulpix0412 2026-10-17T18:06:10Z | closed 2026-10-17T18:10:04Z\n121\t## /code-review findings (T04) and how each was resolved\n122\t\n123\tTwo parallel reviews: **Standards** (CLAUDE.md, CONTEXT.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST, ADRs, plus a code-smell baseline) and **Spec** (this issue, with #1 for context).\n124\t\n125\t### Standards\n126\t| Finding | Resolution |\n127\t|---|---|\n128\t| **Hard:** `.gitignore` line `site/` also ignored `templates/site/`, so the new public-site templates would never be committed and a clean clone's Site build would fail | **Fixed.** Anchored to `/site/`; only the generated output is ignored now |\n129\t| \"This guide has no English **version**\": *version* is an Avoid word | **Fixed.** Reworded to \"has no English text yet\" |\n130\t| Four spellings of one concept (`site_build`, `build_site`, `site_builder`, capability `build_site`) | **Fixed.** `publish.build_site()`, capability `build_site`, dependency `site_builder`, and the route handler is now `update_site` (the 更新网站 button) |\n131\t| Duplicated other-language rule in `publish.py` and `base.html` | **Fixed.** Computed once and passed to templates as `other` |\n132\t| Duplicated \"list or empty notice\" branch in the home and Author templates | **Fixed.** Moved into the `guide_list` macro |\n133\t| Speculative `_Writer(out, **shared)` | **Fixed.** Now an explicit `current_patch` parameter |\n134\t| `site_builder` repeats the shape of `web.admin_user` | **Left as is.** It checks a different capability; a generic `requires(capability)` can come when a third one is needed |\n135\t| Possible Feature Envy: `changes_not_on_site` loads Published Guides to compare times | **Left as is.** It keeps Guide SQL inside `app/guides.py`, and the site is small |\n136\t| Possible Divergent Change in `publish.py`; `lang` as a bare string; unused default deploy message | **Left as is.** Spec #1 places the deploy and the build record with `render_site`. `build_site()` does use the default message |\n137\t\n138\t### Spec\n139\t| Finding | Resolution |\n140\t|---|---|\n141\t| Fallback notice was on the Chinese Guide page instead of the English Hero page the Reader lands on | **Fixed.** The switch links to `en/heroes/<slug>/#no-english-text`, and the English Hero page has a notice with that id that shows only when the Reader arrives through that link (CSS `:target`, no JS). Test updated |\n142\t| \"Newest Guides\" sorted by last edit, so an Admin's typo fix moved an old Guide to the top | **Fixed** (test first). The home page now sorts by publish time |\n143\t| `cms publish` + `cms deploy` from the CLI doesn't reset the \"N 项更改尚未更新到网站\" count | **Known gap.** #1 says \"the CLI commands stay as they are\"; only the 更新网站 button records a Site build |\n144\t| Only a failed deploy is reported; an error while rendering gives a 500 | **Left as is.** A failed push is the expected failure (story 88). A render error is a bug and should show up loudly |\n145\t| Scope: `render_markdown` now drops `href`/`src` values starting with `/`, `//` or `\\` | **Kept.** Without it, a writer's `[x](/foo)` would break the criterion \"No generated file contains `href=\\\"/`\". It applies to the preview too, so the preview still matches the site. A preview warning for this could be added later |\n146\t| The count covers only Published Guides, not Hero or Patch changes | **Known gap.** It meets this ticket's criterion; later tickets (Unpublish, Trash, Pages) extend what counts |\n147\t\n148\tTests: 18 new tests in `tests/test_t04_site_build.py`, covering Seam 2 (`render_site` output) and Seam 1 (the button with the deploy step replaced). Full suite: 139 passed. pyright: 0 errors.\n149\t\n150\t######## #6 T05 — Admins Return or Unpublish Guides with Review notes | Avulpix0412 2026-10-17T19:54:59Z | closed 2026-10-17T20:50:01Z\n151\t## `/code-review` findings for T05 and how each was resolved\n152\t\n153\t| # | Finding | Resolution |\n154\t|---|---------|------------|\n155\t| 1 | **Race:** Return/Unpublish read the status, then wrote it in a separate step. Two Admins acting at once could undo each other's step (e.g. a Guide just Published turned back into a Draft). | **Fixed.** `_send_back` now runs `UPDATE … WHERE id = ? AND status = ?` *first*, with the status that was read. If no row changes, the step is refused (\"这篇攻略刚被别人改过…\") and the transaction rolls back before any review round is written. (`publish` has the same read-then-write shape. That is T03 code, so it is out of scope here.) |\n156\t| 2 | **Overlapping quotes:** a single regex alternation marks the leftmost match, so a second quote overlapping it at a different start was reported as found but never highlighted. | **Fixed.** Each quote is matched on its own, and overlapping spans are merged into one `<mark>`. Test: `test_overlapping_quoted_passages_are_both_highlighted`. |\n157\t| 3 | **`unpublished_since` overcounts:** a Guide Published *and* Unpublished after the last build is counted as a pending change. | **Not changed.** The suggested fix (`published_at <= since`) would *undercount* when a Guide is Unpublished, Published again and Unpublished again after a build. The dashboard would then say \"网站已是最新\" while the Guide is still online. Overcounting only asks for an unneeded rebuild, so it is the safer error. |\n158\t| 4 | **No indexes** on `review_rounds.guide_id` / `review_notes.round_id`, but every Guide query runs a correlated `EXISTS`. | **Fixed.** Added both indexes. |\n159\t| 5 | **The 发布 button sat inside the Review-note form**, so notes typed before pressing it were silently thrown away. | **Fixed.** 发布 now has its own form above the Review note builder, which only Returns or Unpublishes. |\n160\t| 6 | **N+1 in `review_rounds`** (one query per round). | **Fixed.** Now one `LEFT JOIN` query, grouped in Python. |\n161\t| 7 | Quotes are rendered and checked several times per Return. | **Not changed.** These are a few Markdown renders of one Guide on an Admin's click, so the cost is negligible. Caching would make the refusal path harder to follow. |\n162\t| 8 | `review_step` duplicates `workflow_step`. | **Not changed.** They differ on purpose. `workflow_step` saves the editor form and shows the editor on refusal. `review_step` carries Review notes and shows the review screen with the notes kept. Merging them would need a callback for each difference. |\n163\t| 9 | `sent_review_notes` silently dropped non-text fields (e.g. a file posted as `quote`), so Unpublish could go ahead with fewer notes than were sent. | **Fixed.** A non-text field counts as blank, so a half-filled row reaches `app/guides.py` and is refused. Test: `test_a_review_note_sent_as_a_file_is_refused_not_dropped`. |\n164\t\n165\tAfter fixes: pyright 0 errors; `pytest` 170 passed.\n166\t\n167\t\n168\t## Changes made after the review\n169\t\n170\tThese revisions were requested after the review above:\n171\t\n172\t- **Quotes match across formatting** (`a4d3665`). A quoted passage is now matched against the text as Readers see it, ignoring tags and whitespace. A passage copied from the preview is found even when it is part bold, runs through a link, or spans list items or paragraphs. Its highlight is split at each tag it crosses. Line breaks between blocks are never marked, and tags and attributes are copied through unchanged. This replaced finding 2's span merging with one pass over the whole text. Overlapping quotes are still marked together.\n173\t- **Every review round is highlighted** (`a4d3665`). The preview now highlights passages quoted in every round, not just the latest, wherever they are still in the text. Once the Guide is Published again, nothing is highlighted: by then the notes have been dealt with.\n174\t- **The latest round is set apart** (next commit). The latest round's quotes get a solid `<mark>`. Earlier rounds' quotes get `<mark class=\"earlier\">`, a faint tint with a dotted underline, so the two differ without relying on colour. Where they overlap, the latest round wins. The preview shows a key to both. Checked in light and dark mode.\n175\t\n176\tTests added: `test_a_quoted_passage_that_crosses_bold_text_is_found_and_highlighted`, `test_a_quoted_passage_that_crosses_a_link_is_found_and_highlighted`, `test_quoted_passages_from_every_round_are_highlighted_while_still_in_the_text`, `test_the_latest_rounds_highlight_wins_where_it_overlaps_an_earlier_one`. After these changes: pyright 0 errors; `pytest` 174 passed.\n177\t\n178\t\n179\t######## #6 T05 — Admins Return or Unpublish Guides with Review notes | Avulpix0412 2026-10-17T20:48:07Z | closed 2026-10-17T20:50:01Z\n180\tAfter the first round, I let Claude code do two revisions, .Firstly, quotes have to match when they cross formatting. I can imagine that most admins are not expert on computers, so when they review a guide, they will typically copy straight from the preview, so the terms or the links from it will be copied along with other words, with the old rule such return would just be refused, and the admin probably don't know why, and they will just give up and message the editor in the fan group instead, which leaves the review notes unrecorded.\n181\tSecondly, I want to make sure that the quotes from every round is highlighted rather than only the latest. Typically a long guide can easily go back and forth two or three times, so with the old rule if the editor missed something from round 1 and the admin didn't repeat it in round 2, the old highlight would disappear and the problem could easily end up in the published guide. So my choice is to keep all rounds visible, and with the newest round standing out, which will not confused the editor which has been dealt with already and which is still yet to solved.\n182\t\n183\t######## #7 T06 — Editors revise or delete their Published Guides | Avulpix0412 2026-10-17T21:18:03Z | closed 2026-10-18T00:26:41Z\n184\t## `/code-review` findings for T06 and how each was resolved\n185\t\n186\t| # | Finding | Resolution |\n187\t|---|---------|------------|\n188\t| 1 | **No migration:** the new columns (`guides.trashed_at`, `restored_at`, `review_rounds.revision_id`) never reach a database made before T06, and the new index fails on every connect (`no such column: revision_id`). The local `cms.db` from T05 would 500 on every page. | **Fixed.** `db.connect()` now adds any missing column listed in `ADDED_COLUMNS` (`ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN`) before creating indexes on them. To keep every change additive, a Revision's Return is now `kind = 'return'` with `revision_id` set, rather than a new `kind`, since a CHECK can't be altered in place. `revision_id` has no foreign key, and Revision ids are never reused (`AUTOINCREMENT`). Test: `test_a_database_made_before_revisions_and_the_trash_still_works`. Also checked on a copy of the T05 `cms.db`. |\n189\t| 2 | **A Revision can undo newer changes:** it is copied from the Guide when opened, so Publishing it later replaces an Admin's direct edit, or a Guide that was Unpublished, changed and Published again. | **Fixed, as a warning.** A Revision records the Guide's `updated_at` when it is opened. If the Guide changed since, the review screen and the Revision editor say so (\"在这份修订打开之后，攻略又被修改过…发布…那些修改会丢失\"). The Admin decides. Refusing outright would leave the Editor stuck with no way to bring the Revision up to date. Test: `test_the_review_screen_warns_when_the_guide_changed_after_the_revision_opened`. |\n190\t| 3 | **Pending count misses a deletion for good:** a Published Guide deleted to the Trash and then deleted for good before the next build vanishes from `changes_not_on_site`, while the site still shows it. | **Fixed.** Deleting a Published Guide for good records it in a new `removed_guides` table, which the count includes. Deleting and restoring between builds still counts as a change. That overcounts, the safer error, as in T05. Test: `test_deleting_a_published_guide_for_good_stays_a_change_not_on_the_site`. |\n191\t| 4 | **Unpublish silently turns a Submitted Revision back into a Draft** without touching its `updated_at`. | **Fixed** (`updated_at` now moves, and only a Submitted Revision is touched). Keeping the Revision is deliberate: there is nothing for it to change while the Guide is off the site, so it can't be Submitted until the Guide is Published again (\"修订只能在攻略重新发布后提交\"). The Editor learns of the Unpublish from the Guide's own Returned badge. Test: `test_unpublishing_a_guide_holds_its_revision_until_it_is_published_again`. |\n192\t| 5 | **A Revision can't be discarded:** once opened it blocks a new one forever; the only way out was deleting the whole Guide. | **Fixed.** The Author can 放弃修订 after a confirmation step. The Published Guide is untouched, and the Revision's Returns stay in the Guide's history, labelled 退回修订. Test: `test_the_author_discards_their_revision_and_can_open_a_new_one`. |\n193\t| 6 | **An Editor's Published Guide still showed an editable form** whose 保存 always failed with 403. | **Fixed.** `guides.can_edit` decides both the form and `save`. Merging would need a flag at each step, as with `review_step` in T05. |\n198\t\n199\t### Decisions not spelled out in the spec\n200\t\n201\t- Only the Author opens a Revision. Test: `test_a_banned_editor_keeps_drafting_but_submit_and_revisions_are_refused_with_the_reason`. |\n309\t| 2 | `ban_submissions`, `lift_submission_ban` and `reactivate` read the state with one query, then UPDATE without re-checking it, so a change another Admin makes in between (e.g. a Deactivation) could be overwritten. | **Fixed.** Each UPDATE repeats its precondition in the WHERE clause (`AND state = …`, `AND role = 'editor'`), and refuses when no row changes (`CHANGED_MEANWHILE`). Test: `test_an_admin_cannot_deactivate_themselves`. |\n317\t| 10 | Templates hard-coded `minlength=\"8\"` and \"至少 8 个字符\". | **Fixed.** `min_password_length` is a template global from `accounts.MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH`, used on the Users page, the account page and first-login setup. |\n318\t\n319\tThe review also confirmed these hold:\n320\t- the removed T01 deactivation test is covered by T09's test through the real Users page;\n321\t- nothing calls the removed `set_state` any more;\n322\t- every new form carries the CSRF token, and every new link is relative;\n323\t- no password is logged or flashed;\n324\t- `users.last_login_at` is in `ADDED_COLUMNS`.\n325\t\n326\t## Decisions not spelled out in the spec\n327\t\n328\t- **Temporary passwords are typed by the Admin** (at least 8 characters), when creating an account and when resetting a password. The server never shows or stores one in plain text.\n329\t- **A password reset** also ends the user's open sessions. An Admin can't reset their own password. Before T09, only Submit checked the ban.\n332\t- **Reactivating an account returns it to the normal state.** A ban from before the deactivation is not kept, and the confirmation page says so.\n333\t- **The last-active-Admin guard is part of the database update itself.** No console request can reach it: an Admin able to act is active, so the target is never the last Admin. It protects against two Admins removing each other at the same moment. The user agreed to this exception to Seam 1.\n336\t- **Editors refused on Admin routes** now get a console page (403) that keeps the navigation and logout, not plain text.\n337\t- **Users page Guide counts** show \"已发布 N · 共 M\", where M counts Guides in every status outside the Trash.\n338\t- **Last-login times are UTC**, like every other console timestamp.\n339\t- **Schema:** `users.last_login_at` was added the additive way. Test: `test_deactivating_an_account_ends_its_open_session`. |\n| The temporary password could be \"replaced\" by itself during First-login setup (story 5) | Spec | Setup refuses it with 新密码不能与临时密码相同. Test: `test_display_names_are_unique_regardless_of_letter_case`. |\n\n### Fixed (no behaviour change)\n\n- **Test names used avoided words** (`visitor`, `user`). Renamed them to the CONTEXT.md vocabulary. They're all console plumbing, and the docstring says so. Split it if it grows.\n\n### Verification\n\n- `uv run pytest`: the 28 T00 + T01 tests pass. The T00 tests are unchanged.\n- The 14 remaining failures are the course's unfinished exercises (`decide()`, `spend()`), and they failed the same way before this ticket.\n- `pyright` reports 0 errors.\n- A live smoke test on uvicorn, seeded from `.env.example`, covered login (303 to the dashboard, greeted by Display name), logout without a token (403), logout (303), and the dashboard after logout (303 to `/login`). A combined pattern would also need care with overlapping nicknames. |\n| 9 | The nickname storage format was written out in three places. | **Fixed.** One `_to_store` helper. |\n| 10 | `add_hero` and `add_term` repeat the insert-then-reselect pattern, and the import chooses between them with `partial`. | **Not changed.** Heroes differ in their slug and their clash rules, and the two functions are short. |\n\n## Decisions not spelled out in the ticket\n\nAsked and answered this session:\n- **CSV format:** a header row `kind,name_zh,name_en,nicknames` (the nicknames column may be left out). `kind` may be written in English (`item`) or Chinese (`物品`). The new console and site pages were checked with `/browse` at 1280px and 390px: `scrollWidth` is 390 on every page at 390px.\n\n\n######## #10 T09 — Admins manage users | Avulpix0412 2026-10-18T01:08:45Z | closed 2026-10-18T01:16:17Z\n## `/code-review` findings for T09, and how each was resolved\n\nThe review covered the uncommitted T09 work: the Users page, the account page, the lockout guards and the console 403 page.\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | `can_open_revision` (and `can_submit`) still offer the 修订 / 提交审核 buttons to a banned Editor, who is then refused. | **Kept the buttons, as designed:** story 76 wants a banned Editor told *why*, not left with a button that silently went missing. If it ever matters, it is a one-line change. |\n| 8 | Every account mutator re-read and returned the account, and the only caller threw it away. | **Fixed.** The mutators return `None`. |\n| 9 | `GET /admin/users/{id}/deactivate` showed \"are you sure?\" even for yourself or an account already Deactivated, and posting it was then refused. | **Fixed.** `accounts.check_deactivatable` refuses before the confirmation, and the account page is shown with the reason (400). Test: `test_an_admin_cannot_deactivate_themselves`. |\n| 10 | Templates hard-coded `minlength=\"8\"` and \"至少 8 个字符\". | **Fixed.** `min_password_length` is a template global from `accounts.MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH`, used on the Users page, the account page and first-login setup. |\n\nThe review also confirmed these hold:\n- the removed T01 deactivation test is covered by T09's test through the real Users page;\n- nothing calls the removed `set_state` any more;\n- every new form carries the CSRF token, and every new link is relative;\n- no password is logged or flashed;\n- `users.last_login_at` is in `ADDED_COLUMNS`.\n\n## Decisions not spelled out in the spec\n\n- **Temporary passwords are typed by the Admin** (at least 8 characters), when creating an account and when resetting a password. The server never shows or stores one in plain text.\n- **A password reset** also ends the user's open sessions. An Admin can't reset their own password. First-login setup then offers the user's current Display name, so a reset doesn't force a new one.\n- **A Submission ban is for Editors only**, since Admins Publish without Submitting. To promote a banned Editor, the ban must be lifted first.\n- **A banned Editor can't open a Revision** either, because they could never Submit it. Before T09, only Submit checked the ban.\n- **Reactivating an account returns it to the normal state.** A ban from before the deactivation is not kept, and the confirmation page says so.\n- **The last-active-Admin guard is part of the database update itself.** No console request can reach it: an Admin able to act is active, so the target is never the last Admin. {"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"9ee78a2f-b1d4-4b36-9a44-110cd9a16130","hash":"671bbed66055d38b38b2552a38bbe3be8c57c3bc0eab44b2e1923920b5fcabbd","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01RVoUC5TDw8a5EBhQGPxT8g","type":"tool_result","content":"--- line 445\n好,就按你说的来。我会尽量直译、保留你原来的口吻,不润色。润色得越多,越像 AI 写的。\n\n**专有名词的标注方式:** WordPress 界面里的功能名用 **粗体** 标出来。粗体在 Markdown 里本来就合理,你改完可以直接保留,不用再删。\n\n--- line 451\n已经写进 `notes/cms-field-notes.md`,替换了中文版,还没有提交。\n\n**你改的时候留意这几处:**\n\n- **第 3 条**:\"color schemes\" 在 WordPress 新版界面里可能叫 **Styles** 或 **palette**。我不确定你看到的确切叫法,请按你屏幕上的名字改。\n- **第 5 条**:你原话是\"只要前面是 wordpress.net,/ 后面放什么都可以\"。我改成了\"the site address\",因为 Playground 的地址其实是 `playground.wordpress.net`。如果你想保留原意,可以改回去。\n- **第 8 条**:**Shop** 是我猜的名字,请按界面上实际显示的改。\n- **第 11 条**:你说直接输网址时\"找不到网页\"。\"找不到\"和\"拒绝访问\"其实是两回事:WordPress 拒绝时一般会显示 \"Sorry, you are not allowed to access this page\",而\"找不到\"可能只是网址输错了。Playground 的网址前面经常带一段很长的前缀,很容易输错。我写的是 \"couldn't get to it at all\",两种情况都说得通。如果你记得屏幕上的原话,写进去会更好。\n- **第 12 条**:密码泄露的原因,我上一条解释过了。要不要把你的猜测写进去,由你决定,我没加。\n\n**有两个你本来就疑惑的问题,我顺便告诉你答案,要不要写进去你决定:**\n- **违禁词**:WordPress 的规则是一行一个词。输入框旁边应该有一行小字说明,写的是 \"One word or IP address per line\"。\n- **头像**:是根据用户邮箱算出一个固定的图案,同一个邮箱永远得到同一个头像,所以不是真正的随机。\n\n**最后一点:** 这份笔记现在是我翻译的,建议你至少按自己的说法改几句,再在 README 的 AI Use Statement 里写明\"field notes 原文是中文,由 Claude 翻译后我修改\"。这样诚实,而且评分项 A4 本来就要求写清楚你怎么用的 AI。\n\n改完告诉我,下一步是客户简介(`notes/client-brief.md`)。想好选谁了吗?\n\n-----\n--- line 32\n我先看一下你的设置文件里的 model 配置。\n\n--- line 45\n对,你的默认还是 Sonnet。`~/.claude/settings.json` 第 5 行写的是 `\"model\": \"sonnet\"`,环境变量 `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` 没设置,项目级设置里也没有覆盖。\n\n`/model` 显示 \"Kept model as `Sonnet 5.5`\",意思是你没改动,模型仍是 Sonnet 5.5。`sonnet` 这个别名现在指向 Sonnet 5.5,所以没有任何变化。","is_error":false}]}}

Fill this in before your first /implement.)\n\n**Written late.** This plan was written on 2026-10-17, after T04 closed, not\nbefore the first /implement as the manual asks. The upside is that the numbers\nbelow are measured from `notes/usage-ledger.csv`, not guessed.\n\n## Decision\n\nKeep using **Opus 5.5 at high effort** for every remaining ticket (T05–T09, S1, S2).\n\n- Opus 5.5 has done a noticeably better job than Sonnet on this project, so I\n  am not dropping to Sonnet or lowering effort to save budget.\n- If I hit the 5-hour limit, I will **upgrade my plan** rather than switch\n  models or wait it out. I also use Claude Code for other courses (e.g. my IPHS 484\n  project), so the higher plan is worth it beyond this\n  project.\n\n## What tickets have cost so far\n\nPer-ticket cost = sum of the row-to-row rises in `weekly_pct` (and\n`five_h_pct`) for rows labelled with that ticket. The ledger reports whole\npercent, so each figure is ±1.\n\n| Ticket | Weekly % | 5-hour % | Follow-up fix | Weekly % with follow-up |\n|--------|---------:|---------:|---------------|------------------------:|\n| T01    | 2 | 10 | —         | 2 |\n| T02    | 2 | 12 | —         | 2 |\n| T03    | 3 | 24 | #15 (+1)  | 4 |\n| T04    | 2 | 11 | #18 (+0)  | 2 |\n| **Average** | **2.25** | **14.25** | | **2.5** |\n\nNotes:\n- The weekly window reset during T03 (2026-10-17, between 13:00 and 17:10 UTC).\n  Any usage between the last pre-reset row and the reset is lost, so T03's 3% is\n  a lower bound.\n- `exB` (2% weekly) is course exercise work, not a ticket, and is left out.\n- Pre-ticket stages (research, grill, spec, tickets, plus unlabelled setup) cost\n  16% weekly in total; that was the previous week.\n\n## Projection for the remaining tickets\n\nRemaining: T05, T06, T07, T08, T09, S1, S2 = **7 tickets**.\n\n| | Per ticket | × 7 tickets |\n|---|---:|---:|\n| Base (ticket only) | 2.25% | ≈ 16% |\n| With a follow-up fix like #15 / #18 | 2.5% | ≈ 18% |\n\nWeekly usage is at **6%** now (last ledger row, 2026-10-17 19:02 UTC).\n**Projected weekly total after all 7 tickets: ≈ 22%** (≈ 24% with follow-ups),\nwell under the weekly cap even if S1/S2 (stretch tickets, likely bigger) cost\ndouble.\n\n## Where the limit will actually bite\n\nThe 5-hour window is tighter than the weekly one. A ticket costs about 14% of a\n5-hour window (T03 cost 24%), and the current window was already at 47% after\nT04 and #18. Doing more than about three tickets in one sitting could hit the\n5-hour limit; per the decision above, that is when I upgrade.\n\n## Checkpoints\n\n- Re-read the ledger after each ticket. Each entry gives what\nClaude recommended (➡️), then your answer.\n\n### Overrides with a reason\n\n1. **Patches: no \"may be outdated\" label.** S02 L102, round 1 Q4, 2026-10-16 14:58.\n   ➡️ (c): admins set a Current Patch, and older guides get \"可能已过时\".\n   > I guess b makes sense to me, the problem of option c is that because patch nerfs happens so often and it takes time to finish guides, it is possible that someone posts some guides that are for the previous version, and if none of the cards in the guide is changed, then it is still useful\n   Result: guides show their Patch with no outdated label (spec #1, `CONTEXT.md` **Current Patch**).\n\n2. **Bilingual site, not Chinese only.** S02 L102, round 1 Q6.\n   ➡️ Simplified Chinese for every label.\n   > currently it is designed for only Chinese readers, but as the game is originally in English and has a lot of players who speaks English, it also makes sense to have two languages that users can switch between.\n   Then S02 L133 picked (c), a fully translated English site, over Claude's (b), where only the\n   guide bodies were bilingual:\n   > and besides that, I think c is enough.\n   Result: the `zh/` and `en/` trees (T04).\n\n3. **Tournament guides go under Guides, not a Mode field.** S02 L133, round 2 Q1.\n   ➡️ every Guide gets a Mode (Standard / Tournament).\n   > I guess no one will actually make a guides for tournament, so I think if anyone are willing to make it, it is also better to be put into the guide section, so users go to the tournament section to find infos will not be confused.\n\n4. **A Revision keeps the live guide up.** S02 L133, round 2 Q6.\n   ➡️ (b): an edit sends the guide back to Submitted, and it drops off the site. Claude\n   called (c) \"much more work\".\n   > for question 6, option c , for your question, my answer is the author can update the guide if they like and that will replace the old one, don;t show both\n   Result: T06 Revisions.\n\n5. **The language switch moves the whole site.** S02 L152, round 3 Q7.\n   ➡️ list Chinese-only guides on the English site with a language badge.\n   > I think the web should have a switch button on the top right of the page that users can switch the langauge of the whole site, and all the contents including the web and the guides will stay in one language\n\n6. **Tournament mode is in the game, and announcements and recaps are separate items.** S02 L180, round 4 Q1.\n   ➡️ (b): one entry per tournament, updated from announcement into recap.\n   > for question 1, I choose c  and remember that tournament is a game mode inside the game, not some matches that players organize themselves\n\n7. **Editors may delete their own Published guides.** S02 L180, round 4 Q6.\n   ➡️ \"editors can't delete their own Published guides\".\n   > for question 6, editors can definitely delete their own pulished guides, you should change that\n   Result: deleted guides go to the Trash (T06).\n\n8. **A Submission ban doesn't hide an editor's guides.** S02 L211, round 5 Q2.\n   ➡️ asked whether a ban should \"hide all their Published guides at once\".\n   > no, a ban should not hide all published guides at once, because it is not likely that all the guides are harmful, so it is better to do that separately\n\n9. **The hosted console: you chose it, then accepted Claude's pushback.** S02 L234, round 5 Q5:\n   you picked (b), a hosted console. At S02 L270, Claude pointed out that it conflicts with\n   ADR-001 and `CLAUDE.md`:\n   > for question one, you are right and I choose option a\n   Result: the hosted console became stretch ticket #12, which you are not doing.\n\n### Client facts the question didn't contain\n\n10. **Tournament size.** S02 L102, round 1 Q2:\n    > in the tournament, multiple (can up to 50 or even 100)players play at the same time in one game and will have a champion in the end.\n11. **The 52poke wiki as the reason to leave out a card database.** S02 L102, round 1 Q1:\n    > (you can consider the example of wiki.52poke.com for pokemon)\n12. **Patch as a guide field (you raised it before Claude did).** S02 L102, round 1 Q3:\n    > Also this remind me that it is also better to let the edtior also indicates what the version of the game they are giving guides on, for example, 6.7, because after each patch, the environment of the game will be totally different\n13. **Hero nicknames.** S02 L133, round 2 Q2. Each entry gives what\nClaude recommended (➡️), then your answer.\n\n### Overrides with a reason\n\n1. **Patches: no \"may be outdated\" label.** S02 L102, round 1 Q4, 2026-10-16 14:58.\n   ➡️ (c): admins set a Current Patch, and older guides get \"可能已过时\".\n   > I guess b makes sense to me, the problem of option c is that because patch nerfs happens so often and it takes time to finish guides, it is possible that someone posts some guides that are for the previous version, and if none of the cards in the guide is changed, then it is still useful\n   Result: guides show their Patch with no outdated label (spec #1, `CONTEXT.md` **Current Patch**).\n\n2. **Bilingual site, not Chinese only.** S02 L102, round 1 Q6.\n   ➡️ Simplified Chinese for every label.\n   > currently it is designed for only Chinese readers, but as the game is originally in English and has a lot of players who speaks English, it also makes sense to have two languages that users can switch between.\n   Then S02 L133 picked (c), a fully translated English site, over Claude's (b), where only the\n   guide bodies were bilingual:\n   > and besides that, I think c is enough.\n   Result: the `zh/` and `en/` trees (T04).\n\n3. **Tournament guides go under Guides, not a Mode field.** S02 L133, round 2 Q1.\n   ➡️ every Guide gets a Mode (Standard / Tournament).\n   > I guess no one will actually make a guides for tournament, so I think if anyone are willing to make it, it is also better to be put into the guide section, so users go to the tournament section to find infos will not be confused.\n\n4. **A Revision keeps the live guide up.** S02 L133, round 2 Q6.\n   ➡️ (b): an edit sends the guide back to Submitted, and it drops off the site. Claude\n   called (c) \"much more work\".\n   > for question 6, option c , for your question, my answer is the author can update the guide if they like and that will replace the old one, don;t show both\n   Result: T06 Revisions.\n\n5. **The language switch moves the whole site.** S02 L152, round 3 Q7.\n   ➡️ list Chinese-only guides on the English site with a language badge.\n   > I think the web should have a switch button on the top right of the page that users can switch the langauge of the whole site, and all the contents including the web and the guides will stay in one language\n\n6. **Tournament mode is in the game, and announcements and recaps are separate items.** S02 L180, round 4 Q1.\n   ➡️ (b): one entry per tournament, updated from announcement into recap.\n   > for question 1, I choose c  and remember that tournament is a game mode inside the game, not some matches that players organize themselves\n\n7. **Editors may delete their own Published guides.** S02 L180, round 4 Q6.\n   ➡️ \"editors can't delete their own Published guides\".\n   > for question 6, editors can definitely delete their own pulished guides, you should change that\n   Result: deleted guides go to the Trash (T06).\n\n8. **A Submission ban doesn't hide an editor's guides.** S02 L211, round 5 Q2.\n   ➡️ asked whether a ban should \"hide all their Published guides at once\".\n   > no, a ban should not hide all published guides at once, because it is not likely that all the guides are harmful, so it is better to do that separately\n\n9. **The hosted console: you chose it, then accepted Claude's pushback.** S02 L234, round 5 Q5:\n   you picked (b), a hosted console. At S02 L270, Claude pointed out that it conflicts with\n   ADR-001 and `CLAUDE.md`:\n   > for question one, you are right and I choose option a\n   Result: the hosted console became stretch ticket #12, which you are not doing.\n\n### Client facts the question didn't contain\n\n10. **Tournament size.** S02 L102, round 1 Q2:\n    > in the tournament, multiple (can up to 50 or even 100)players play at the same time in one game and will have a champion in the end.\n11. **The 52poke wiki as the reason to leave out a card database.** S02 L102, round 1 Q1:\n    > (you can consider the example of wiki.52poke.com for pokemon)\n12. **Patch as a guide field (you raised it before Claude did).** S02 L102, round 1 Q3:\n    > Also this remind me that it is also better to let the edtior also indicates what the version of the game they are giving guides on, for example, 6.7, because after each patch, the environment of the game will be totally different\n13. **Hero nicknames.** S02 L133, round 2 Q2. This became the nickname warnings in T07:\n    > I know for Chinese there are some nicknames for each hero, and it is better to just use the official name\n14. **Only two older patches.** S02 L133, round 2 Q3:\n    > I don't think anyone will be posting anything more than 2 versions before\n15. **Marking the part of a guide that failed review.** S02 L133, round 2 Q5. Claude had\n    proposed a short note; this became Review notes with quoted passages (T05):\n    > the editor can also highlight the section that is not approved and advice for further revision.\n16. **Official names stored in pairs.** S02 L133, the answer you numbered 7, which became Game Terms (T07):\n    > all the things that can be mistranslated all have their official names, for example skills, we can stored all of that in pairs in the website\n17. **How many Game Terms there are.** S02 L152, round 3 Q5:\n    > I mean skills, along with items, enchantments, and monsters, there are thousands of them\n18. **Merchants and events.** S02 L180, round 4 Q2:\n    > card and items are the same thing, you are right that merchants and events are additional terms.\n19. **Stopping an account from publishing.** S02 L180, round 4 Q7. This became the Submission ban (T09):\n    > admins should also be able to see a user page that lists all the editors and they could have some actions for each editors, for example, stop the account from publishing any guides\n\n### Decisions after the grill (also yours, with dates)\n\n- **A Hero's Slug stays fixed** (S06 L9, 2026-10-17 17:34). This reversed what Claude built in\n  T02, which the T02 review had flagged \"as a decision to confirm\". It became #15, and your\n  reason is in your comment on #15.\n- **The console templates are not exempt** from the path check (S11 L77, 2026-10-17 18:43). See (b)1.\n- **Review quotes match across formatting, and every round is highlighted** (S13 L762,\n  2026-10-17 20:26). The reasons are in your comment on #6.\n- **T09 before T07, against Claude's recommendation.** Your comment on #25, 2026-10-18 01:17.\n- **One-character Chinese nicknames: a notice, not a refusal** (S16 L1180, 2026-10-18 02:11).\n  Your comment on #8.\n- **Before the grill, in Chinese**, the client brief's facts. S01 L620, 2026-10-16 04:36, says\n  patches land about twice a month:\n  > 对于特定版本，我想补充的是游戏因为平衡性原因经常会有平衡补丁调整卡牌强弱，平均一个月会有两回\n\n---\n\n## (b) Where the AI drifted or invented something, and what caught it\n\nOrdered by how well each fits G1(b): a named ticket, the drifted claim quoted, and the step\nthat caught it.\n\n1. **#18: Claude read your request backwards and proposed weakening the grader's check.**\n   (S11, 2026-10-17 18:38–18:49.) You asked for an issue saying the console templates are\n   *not* exempt from the root-absolute-path check. Claude's issue proposed the opposite (S11 L71):\n   > **Suggested fix in the issue:** narrow which files the check scans by adding `':(exclude)templates/admin/**'`, or by listing only the directories that get published.\n   **Caught by:** you, reading the issue (S11 L77):\n   > Don't change scripts/check_submission.py. the console templates are NOT exempt from the no-root-absolute-paths rule\n   Claude then replied \"I had it backwards.\" (S11 L82) and named the cause: `CLAUDE.md` said\n   \"**Published** HTML uses relative paths only\". You had that line changed to \"All committed\n   HTML\" (S11 L104), and #18 fixed the templates.\n\n2. **S1 (#11), PR #29: two test claims in the PR description didn't match the tests.**\n   (S20, 2026-10-18 05:59.) The draft said:\n   > SVG, \\\"notes.txt\\\" renamed .png, 5 MB + 1 byte → refused; exactly 5 MB → accepted\n\n   > another Editor's Guide → 403/404 for upload, delete and v…\n\n   The tests actually use an SVG or a PDF named `.png`, and someone else's Guide answers 404, not 403.\n   **Caught by:** checking each claim against `tests/test_s1_images.py` before merging (S20\n   L1376 and L1417), the habit handoff 07 records. Fixed before the merge.\n\n3. **S1 (#11): glossary drift.** Review finding 10 on #11:\n   > The glossary listed \"media\" and \"thumbnail\" under _Avoid_, yet the code uses them.\n   **Caught by:** `/code-review`, checking the code against `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n4. **T04 (#5): one ignore rule would have broken a clean clone.** Review on #5 (Standards, marked \"Hard\"):\n   > `.gitignore` line `site/` also ignored `templates/site/`, so the new public-site templates would never be committed and a clean clone's Site build would fail\n   **Caught by:** `/code-review`. The same review also found an Avoid word, \"no English\n   **version**\" (`CONTEXT.md`), and the fallback notice on the wrong page (the Spec axis).\n\n5. **T07 (#8): a docstring claimed something the code didn't do.** Finding 4:\n   > Re-running the seed called the full import, which would overwrite names an Admin had since edited. The review on #3 listed it as:\n   > A slug is re-derived when the English name is edited | **Kept, as a decision to confirm.**\n   **Caught by:** `/code-review` surfaced it, and you reversed it in #15 (S06 L9).\n\n9. **Field notes, before the grill (S01, 2026-10-15).** You asked for English drafts to edit\n   yourself. Claude wrote them straight into `notes/cms-field-notes.md` and replaced your\n   Chinese text (S01 L451: \"已经写进 `notes/cms-field-notes.md`,替换了中文版\"). **Caught by:** you (S01 L460):\n   > 你没搞清楚状况，我不是让你直接改，我是让你把英文草稿先给我，然后我改完之后你再放进去\n   Claude also flagged its own guesses in that draft (S01 L451: \"**Shop** 是我猜的名字\").\n   This is an instruction-following failure rather than an invented fact. Readers, who have no\n+account, find a written build for a given Hero and Patch on the public site\n+instead of scrubbing through videos.\n \n-## Start here\n+The admin console runs on a laptop only. `cms publish` renders the published\n+content into `site/` as static HTML in Chinese and English, and that is what\n+GitHub Pages serves. The project's vocabulary is in `CONTEXT.md`.\n \n-1. `docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md` — the manual. Read Part 0 and Part 1 first.\n-2. `docs/mp2-grading-rubric_20260922.md` — how you are graded. Read it **before** you build.\n-3. `docs/mp2-setup_context-threshold-hook_20260922.md` — Exercise A, in Part 4 of the manual.\n+## Live URL\n \n-## Run it\n+https://avulpix0412.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n+\n+## Run locally\n+\n+Needs [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Python 3.12 or newer.\n \n ```bash\n+git clone https://github.com/Avulpix0412/iphs400-mp2-cms.git\n+cd iphs400-mp2-cms\n uv sync\n cp .env.example .env    # then change the passwords and the secret key\n-uv run --env-file .env python scripts/seed_demo.py   # demo accounts, Heroes, Patches\n-uv run --env-file .env cms serve   # then open http://localhost:8000/login\n+uv run --env-file .env python scripts/seed_demo.py\n+uv run --env-file .env cms serve    # then open http://localhost:8000/login\n ```\n \n-The seeded accounts are `admin@example.test` (Admin, 演示管理员) and\n+Keep `--env-file .env` on every command: the app and the seed script read their\n+settings from the environment and do not load `.env` themselves. Quote any value\n+that contains spaces. uv rejects the whole file if one line does not parse, and\n+the seed script then reports the passwords as missing.\n+\n+The seed script creates `admin@example.test` (Admin, 演示管理员) and\n `editor@example.test` (Editor, 演示编辑), with the passwords you set in `.env` as\n-`CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD`. The seed script refuses to run\n-without them; there are no default passwords. It also adds a few demo Heroes\n-and the Patches 6.5–6.7, with 6.7 as the Current Patch (管理后台 → 英雄 / 版本).\n-\n-## What is here\n-\n-```text\n-.claude/hooks/     the context meter and usage ledger (Exercise A lives in ctx_guard.py)\n-scripts/           usage_report.py (Exercise B lives in spend()), check_submission.py, seed_demo.py\n-tests/             the exercise tests, plus helpers such as client_as(\"editor\")\n-app/, templates/   the T00 skeleton — every CMS feature is yours to build\n-docs/adr/          two example decision records\n+`CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD`. It refuses to run without them;\n+there are no default passwords. It also adds demo Heroes, the Patches 6.5–6.7\n+(6.7 is the Current Patch), Draft, Submitted and Published Guides, an About\n+page and two Tournament items. Running it again leaves existing records unchanged.\n+\n+To build the public site from what is published:\n+\n+```bash\n+uv run --env-file .env cms publish    # writes site/; it prints a preview command\n ```\n \n-Two functions are deliberately unfinished and their tests fail until you write them:\n-`decide()` in `.claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py` and `spend()` in `scripts/usage_report.py`.\n-Both are graded. Use `/tdd`, as the manual says.\n+## Generative AI Use Statement\n \n-## Deadlines\n+Models (all through Anthropic):\n \n-Stage 1 (`mp2-mvp` tag): Tue Sep 29, 2:40 pm Eastern (soft target).\n-Stage 2 (`mp2-final` tag): Tue Oct 6, 2:40 pm Eastern, grace until Wed Oct 7, 2:40 pm.\n+- Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`): every session.\n+- Claude Sonnet 5.5 (`claude-sonnet-5-5`): part of the first session, 2026-10-12.\n \n-Run `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2` before you submit.\n+Skills:\n \n-## Generative AI Use Statement\n+- mattpocock-skills: `grill-with-docs`, `grilling` and `domain-modeling` (the\n+  grill); `to-spec` and `to-tickets`; `implement` and `tdd` (each ticket);\n+  `code-review`; `pr`; `handoff`; `research`.\n+- Claude Code's built-in `/code-review`.\n+- gstack `/browse`, for checking pages in a headless browser and taking the\n+  screenshots.\n+\n+### Backends used\n+\n+| Provider | Models | Ledger sessions | Ledger rows | Dates |\n+|---|---|---|---|---|\n+| Anthropic | Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 | 22 | 130 (Opus 119, Sonnet 11) | 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-18 |\n \n-*(Required. Replace this section: name the models and skills you used, quote two\n-prompts you really sent, describe one real model failure, and include a\n-\"Backends used\" table if you ever switched providers.)*\n+No session used a non-Anthropic base URL, so no commit carries a `Backend:` trailer.\n-----\n1\n0\n M .env.example\n M README.md\n M notes/usage-ledger.csv\n?? docs/handoff/08_screenshots-to-writing_20261018.md\n?? docs/transcripts/iphs400_mp2-cms_chat-session_21_nick-chen_20261018.md","is_error":false}]}}

From `notes/usage-ledger.csv`, T01 is **8** and T03 is\n    **21** under the plan's own method (every rise credited to the later row's phase). Under\n    `scripts/usage_report.py`'s method they are 8 and 12. The plan's caveat \"each figure is ±1\"\n    doesn't cover a 2–3 point gap, while the weekly column (2, 2, 3, 2) matches exactly. {"parentUuid":"3de8d2ba-ec73-4e99-bd80-c025767a9f4d","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg9QmH9t9ZEkq46283vNk","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_019FuSyZEHGBfv6wCAMNWjCB","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"B=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/9ee78a2f-b1d4-4b36-9a44-110cd9a16130/scratchpad/issue-dotenv.md; cat > $B <<'EOF'\n## Problem\n\nThe app and `scripts/seed_demo.py` read their settings only from the process\nenvironment (`app/settings.py`, `scripts/seed_demo.py:154`). Neither loads `.env`, so\nevery command needs `uv run --env-file .env …`.\n\nThe rubric's judge doesn't do that. Rubric §10 T3 runs:\n\n```bash\nuv sync && cp .env.example .env\nuv run python scripts/seed_demo.py\nuv run cms serve --port 8000 &\n```\n\nOn a fresh clone of `main` (`9f96c2b`, tested 2026-10-18), the second line fails with exit 1:\n\n```text\nSet CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD in .env (copy .env.example), then run `uv run --env-file .env python scripts/seed_demo.py`.\n```\n\nWith no seeded accounts, the judge can't log in for the walkthrough, which puts C (15 pts)\nat risk. E4 (\"`scripts/seed_demo.py` runs clean from `.env.example` values with no manual\nsteps\") fails too. `cms serve` would start, but with the default secret key and site title.\n\n## What to do\n\n- The seed script and the console (`cms serve`, and the rest of the `cms` command) load\n  `.env` themselves, so `uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py` and `uv run cms serve` work\n  without `--env-file`.\n- **Variables already set in the environment win** over `.env`. The tests set\n  `CMS_DATABASE` and friends per test, so loading `.env` must never override them.\n  `uv run --env-file .env …` keeps working too.\n- A missing `.env` is not an error: the current behaviour, and the seed's message, stay.\n- **Standard library only.** No `python-dotenv` (the stack in `pyproject.toml` is fixed).\n  The parser needs to handle what `.env.example` uses: `KEY=value`, `KEY=\"quoted value\"`,\n  blank lines and `#` comments.\n- The README's *Run locally* section is updated to match.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] On a fresh clone: `uv sync`, `cp .env.example .env`, `uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`\n      seeds the demo accounts, and `uv run cms serve` serves `/login`.\n- [ ] A variable set in the environment beats the same key in `.env` (test).\n- [ ] No `.env` file: the seed prints its existing message and exits 1 (test).\n- [ ] Quoted values with spaces, comments and blank lines parse (test).\n- [ ] The full suite passes unchanged, and no test cat > $B <<'EOF'\n## Problem\n\nThe app and `scripts/seed_demo.py` read their settings only from the process\nenvironment (`app/settings.py`, `scripts/seed_demo.py:154`). Neither loads `.env`, so\nevery command needs `uv run --env-file .env …`.\n\nThe rubric's judge doesn't do that. Rubric §10 T3 runs:\n\n```bash\nuv sync && cp .env.example .env\nuv run python scripts/seed_demo.py\nuv run cms serve --port 8000 &\n```\n\nOn a fresh clone of `main` (`9f96c2b`, tested 2026-10-18), the second line fails with exit 1:\n\n```text\nSet CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD in .env (copy .env.example), then run `uv run --env-file .env python scripts/seed_demo.py`.\n```\n\nWith no seeded accounts, the judge can't log in for the walkthrough, which puts C (15 pts)\nat risk. E4 (\"`scripts/seed_demo.py` runs clean from `.env.example` values with no manual\nsteps\") fails too. `cms serve` would start, but with the default secret key and site title.\n\n## What to do\n\n- The seed script and the console (`cms serve`, and the rest of the `cms` command) load\n  `.env` themselves, so `uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py` and `uv run cms serve` work\n  without `--env-file`.\n- **Variables already set in the environment win** over `.env`. The tests set\n  `CMS_DATABASE` and friends per test, so loading `.env` must never override them.\n  `uv run --env-file .env …` keeps working too.\n- A missing `.env` is not an error: the current behaviour, and the seed's message, stay.\n- **Standard library only.** No `python-dotenv` (the stack in `pyproject.toml` is fixed).\n  The parser needs to handle what `.env.example` uses: `KEY=value`, `KEY=\"quoted value\"`,\n  blank lines and `#` comments.\n- The README's *Run locally* section is updated to match.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] On a fresh clone: `uv sync`, `cp .env.example .env`, `uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`\n      seeds the demo accounts, and `uv run cms serve` serves `/login`.\n- [ ] A variable set in the environment beats the same key in `.env` (test).\n- [ ] No `.env` file: the seed prints its existing message and exits 1 (test).\n- [ ] Quoted values with spaces, comments and blank lines parse (test).\n- [ ] The full suite passes unchanged, and no test reads the developer's real `.env`.\n\nBlocked by: none\nEOF\ngh issue create --title \"The seed script and the console load .env themselves\" --body-file $B","description":"Open unlabeled issue for loading .env without --env-file"}},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg9QmGpYWmonyhFdYYinj","requestRef":"c810838f-cb7d-424d-870b-ae904fdfceb9","requestedModel":"claude-opus-5-5","type":"assistant","uuid":"8fa0a67e-b6cb-4041-aee8-b7261c3ed73b","timestamp":"2026-10-18T08:46:28.212Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"9ee78a2f-b1d4-4b36-9a44-110cd9a16130","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"9ee78a2f-b1d4-4b36-9a44-110cd9a16130","version":"2.1.302","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}
